name: Huey
notes: St. Louis snap built around a dance-instruction hook, and the one entry in this batch whose *snare roll* is documented rather than approximated. The research says "snare-roll fills into the hook" outright, so `fills.fillBeforeSection` is set explicitly and `snareRoll.gapProb` is 0.12 — the lowest gap in the batch, which is what makes the roll a stream into the downbeat instead of a scatter. Everything else is subtraction: a single chord, a 3-note synth line, `bass808` with `legato` sustain and `slideProb` 0.01 because the research says "no movement", and a chant hook that does the melodic work — which is why `countermelody` leads with `answer_lick` at weight 4 and the melody itself sits at [2, 4] notes a bar with `emptyBarBias` 0.2. ⛔ **`confidence` is low because the research rates this medium-low**: only the era and the lane are sourced, and it says so — "parameters inferred". The specific inferences are `session.bpm` (the 70–80 half-time band carries [LOW-CONF]) and every drum probability below it; the sourced facts are the record, the year, the city and the dance-instruction hook format. ⚠ `chords.progressionFamilies` is a static `i` at weight 8 with an **INFERRED** `i–VII` at weight 2. The research says "minor, single-chord" and that is what the weights say; the neighbour exists only because the chord part is still owed 55 distinct outputs over 200 seeds, and most of that comes from `chordDurationBeats` [4, 16] rather than from changes. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 881 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: styles 3, melody density [2,5]. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [2,1], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
